status: The 23 early-societies records have explicit reviewed authoring dispositions: 21 Full and 2 Partial. The two remaining conditions concern early-period Inuit conflict-resolution evidence, retained for the specific and integrated knowledge expectation. This is a completed bounded review, not complete coverage or pupil attainment.

actions: Use all four prior comparison designs together, retaining their actual three early cultural settings and exact source roles. The learned repertoire includes Droulers around 1450, Qariaraqyuk with substantial 14th-century occupation and separately dated ancient Egyptian cases. The attributed Haudenosaunee founding/social relationship and around 1475 Greenland young-person supplement have their own source/chronology roles; neither silently becomes an eyewitness Droulers or Qari biography.

Have the learner explain selected daily-material, social/work and environmental relationships using their supported actual cases, then compare with actual own-life/class participation and the dated Canadian environmental/provider accounts already prepared. Include meaningful similarities and differences rather than a list of old objects and modern places. Actual familiar present-day work/helping relationships can be described without claiming every Canadian shares one family, role, technology, wealth or environmental practice.

Relate changes and continuities to the selected setting, resources and institutional/role circumstances where supported. Distinguish different perspectives without requiring a personal cultural identity disclosure or ranking societies as better or worse. Use both prior own-life comparison and the actual contemporary Canadian cases; a fictional modern profile alone does not replace self-application.

After the separate whole knowledge checks, use a changed attributed example and explain what comparison the evidence allows and what remains unknown. Preserve source-specific reconstruction, elite representation, period and current-provider limits. No pupil passing result is assumed.
integrated-then-now.positive: Integrates the four source-fit comparison operations, with actual own-life and contemporary Canadian connections and accurate separate cultural/source boundaries.
nearMiss: Lists separate facts but does not make a supported then-now comparison.
Uses one imagined primitive child or one generic Indigenous government.
Treats a reconstructed setting or idealised image as every individual’s documented routine.

actions: Use the reviewed locations/maps, material life, environment and organisation protocols together. Require the actual First Nation, Inuit and Egyptian case knowledge, not only general historical method or a linked-topic count.

Check the supported daily life, setting, authority, social/work and cooperation relationships from the specific tasks, with source-period and uncertainty limits intact. Complete the missing early-period conflict/cooperation source condition before certifying this integrated knowledge expectation as Full. Available authoring evidence supports the other specific designs; no absent topic or learner deficit is inferred.

sourceCases.use: Attributed founding-peace and shared-council relationship addresses conflict and greater cooperation; exact founding date is not asserted.
sourceCases.basis: Source-attributed early founding tradition with uncertain date, distinct from every current policy.

sourceCases.use: The dated early community and qualified leadership/crew-resource reconstruction supports cooperation; not an observed dispute-resolution rule.
sourceCases.basis: Archaeology plus explicit later analogy; a specific early conflict-resolution function is not established.

sourceCases.use: Historical summer camps linked trade, resolving conflicts and alliances; source also discusses pre-European mobility, colonial continuation and separately dated modern revival.
sourceCases.basis: The body does not establish that the conflict-resolution function predates 1500. Precolonial is not automatically pre-1500, and modern revival dates are not historical practice dates.

sourceCases.use: Pharaonic ruler and vizier judicial/administrative offices offer a bounded institutional attempt to maintain order. No invented trial, equal-rights conclusion or successful-resolution frequency.
sourceCases.basis: The selected Pharaonic institutional description falls within the earlier historical scope; it is a survey model, not an eyewitness individual dispute.

actions: Describe the supported institutional aims across the prepared cases: founding peace/shared council, coordinated harvesting/resource relations, and Egyptian judicial/administrative organisation. Separate intended purpose from demonstrated success; cooperation is not proof of no conflict.

Use the Greenland museum account as a clearly attributed historical comparison with its chronology limit. Ask what evidence would be needed to locate the conflict-resolution function in the source’s pre-1500 scope. Do not infer it from an ancient drum fragment, invent a Qari dispute or claim all Inuit communities used one system.

For eventual Full authoring coverage, prepare an accurately attributed early-period Inuit account or a supported historical interpretation of the function, then retain the existing whole knowledge/task checks. An exact dated dispute event is not required; source-supported period fit for an institutional attempt is. No new topic, ceremony or performance reenactment is necessary.
